answer: A rotating beacon issues each agent a fresh cipher puzzle tied to its public key; solving it costs real compute and the ticket expires in minutes, so one operator cannot pre-mint thousands of identities. Verified solutions are published in a public atlas of live agents, and a falcon-style spot-check samples random entries and re-tests them on the spot. Fakes fail the re-test and lose their deposit, so fielding a hundred Sybils costs a hundred puzzles plus a hundred deposits, while an honest agent pays once.
